definitions.explanation: A Japanese condiment consisting of a dry mixture of ingredients such as dried fish flakes, sesame seeds, seaweed, and salt, designed to be sprinkled over cooked rice. A staple of Japanese home cooking, especially popular in bento boxes.

examples.japanese: ごはんにふりかけをかける。
{子|こ}どもはふりかけが{大好|だいす}きだ。
お{弁当|べんとう}の{白|しろ}いごはんにふりかけをかけて{持|も}っていった。
examples.english: I sprinkled furikake on the white rice in my bento and took it with me.

notes: Written in hiragana. Derived from the verb {振|ふ}りかける (to sprinkle). Common flavors include のり{塩|しお} (seaweed salt), {鮭|さけ} (salmon), and たまご (egg). Sold in individual packets or jars at supermarkets. A convenient way to add flavor to plain rice.
